title: Three Things Shown to Adam; First Image; the Two Mysteries
description: What is impressed upon the human, what is worked in the soul by light, what is daily seen. T65 — the three distinctions set upon the human being (divine image, structural pattern of the firstborn, seal of every power), and the seven consequences that follow: why heaven and earth are stirred on the soul's account, and why the self continually presses to draw the light from her. T66 — the seven goods divine truth works in the soul when it shines (sight, peace, wakefulness, nourishment, gathering of beasts to lairs, dissolution of plague, manifestation of the Radiance) — met by seven evils when truth withdraws. T67 — the two visible mysteries: the sun as the likeness of the Father unveiled in his shining, the night as the shadow of the King of Darkness recognized daily by what fills the cosmos when truth is not there.
